surstr-mming.name: Surströmming
surstr-mming.summary: A fermented Baltic herring dish traditional to Swedish cuisine since at least the 16th century, famous for its powerful smell.

great-famine-of-1695-1697.name: Great Famine of 1695–1697
great-famine-of-1695-1697.summary: A famine that struck Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Norway and Sweden in the 1690s, occurring at the same time as Scotland's 'Seven Ill Years' famine.

br-nnvin.name: Brännvin
br-nnvin.summary: Old Nordic term for distilled liquor, typically made from potatoes or grain, with an alcohol content usually between 30% and 38%.

stockfish.name: Stockfish
stockfish.summary: Unsalted fish, especially cod, dried by cold air and wind on wooden racks; one of the oldest food preservation methods, with a storage life of several years.

royal-danish-academy-of-fine-arts.name: Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts
royal-danish-academy-of-fine-arts.summary: An art school that has educated artists in Denmark for more than 250 years, shaping the development of Danish art.
royal-danish-academy-of-fine-arts.source_title: Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts

danish-golden-age.name: Danish Golden Age
danish-golden-age.summary: A period of exceptional Danish creativity, mainly in the first half of the 19th century, spanning painting, architecture, music, literature and science.

johannes-wiedewelt.name: Johannes Wiedewelt
johannes-wiedewelt.summary: Danish neoclassical sculptor (1731–1802) who became court sculptor and introduced neoclassical ideals to Denmark through palace decorations, garden sculptures and memorial monuments.

frederick-v-of-denmark.name: Frederick V of Denmark
frederick-v-of-denmark.summary: King of Denmark and Norway from 1746 to 1766, whose reign saw commerce, art and science flourish even as alcoholism left him reliant on his enlightened ministers.

roskilde-cathedral.name: Roskilde Cathedral
roskilde-cathedral.summary: A Lutheran cathedral in Roskilde, Denmark, built in the 12th–13th centuries and the official burial church of Danish monarchs since the 15th century, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

carl-gustaf-pilo.name: Carl Gustaf Pilo
carl-gustaf-pilo.summary: Swedish painter (1711–1793) who served as court painter in Denmark and led the Royal Danish Academy of Art, renowned for his royal portraits and the painting "The Coronation of Gustaf III".

royal-copenhagen.name: Royal Copenhagen Porcelain Factory
royal-copenhagen.summary: A Danish porcelain manufacturer founded in Copenhagen in 1775 under the protection of Queen Dowager Juliane Marie, known for its three-wavy-line mark symbolizing Denmark's three waterways.

swedish-empire.name: Swedish Empire
swedish-empire.summary: The period of Swedish history, from 1611 to 1721, when Sweden was a European great power controlling much of the Baltic region.

nicolai-abildgaard.name: Nicolai Abildgaard
nicolai-abildgaard.summary: Danish neoclassical painter and professor (1743–1809) who led the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts and developed a Neo-Classical style.

christian-august-lorentzen.name: Christian August Lorentzen
christian-august-lorentzen.summary: Danish painter who lived from 1749 to 1828.

jens-juel-painter.name: Jens Juel
jens-juel-painter.summary: A Danish painter (1745–1802) regarded as the leading Danish portrait painter of the 18th century, with his largest collection of portraits held at Frederiksborg Castle.

kosta-boda.name: Kosta Glasbruk
kosta-boda.summary: Swedish glassmaking company (now Kosta Boda) known for art glass and tableware, based in the town of Kosta, which was named after it; the surrounding 'Kingdom of Crystal' region now draws about a million visitors a year.

alexander-roslin.name: Alexander Roslin
alexander-roslin.summary: An 18th-century Swedish painter (1718–1793) who worked across Europe for aristocratic patrons, blending Classicist and Rococo styles in portraiture.

golden-horns-of-gallehus.name: Golden Horns of Gallehus
golden-horns-of-gallehus.summary: Two elaborately decorated 5th-century gold horns found in Southern Jutland, Denmark, in 1639 and 1734, stolen and melted down in 1802 and known today only through replicas.

northern-seven-years-war.name: Northern Seven Years' War
northern-seven-years-war.summary: War fought from 1563 to 1570 between Sweden and a coalition of Denmark–Norway, Lübeck and Poland–Lithuania, ending in a stalemate with the Treaty of Stettin.

denmark-norway.name: Denmark-Norway
denmark-norway.summary: A real union of the kingdoms of Denmark and Norway (with Norway's overseas possessions) plus Schleswig and Holstein, lasting from the 16th to 19th centuries.

l-beck.name: Lübeck
l-beck.summary: City in northern Germany on the Baltic coast; from the mid-12th century it became the de facto capital of the Hanseatic League.

treaty-of-stettin-1570.name: Treaty of Stettin
treaty-of-stettin-1570.summary: 1570 treaty ending the Northern Seven Years' War between Sweden and a coalition led by Denmark, with neither side gaining territory.

great-northern-war.name: Great Northern War
great-northern-war.summary: A war from 1700 to 1721 in which a coalition led by Russia broke Sweden's dominance over Northern, Central and Eastern Europe, ending with Russia as the region's leading power.

personal-union-of-poland-and-saxony.name: Saxony-Poland
personal-union-of-poland-and-saxony.summary: A personal union between the Electorate of Saxony and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, lasting 1697 to 1706 and 1709 to 1763 under the House of Wettin, remembered in Poland as a disorderly era.
personal-union-of-poland-and-saxony.source_title: Personal union of Poland and Saxony

treaty-of-nystad.name: Treaty of Nystad
treaty-of-nystad.summary: 1721 treaty ending the Great Northern War between Russia and Sweden, transferring Estonia, Livonia and Ingria to Russia.

treaties-of-stockholm-great-northern-war.name: Treaties of Stockholm
treaties-of-stockholm-great-northern-war.summary: Two treaties, signed in 1719 and 1720, ending the war between Sweden and an alliance of Hanover and Prussia following the death of Charles XII.

christian-iv-of-denmark.name: Christian IV of Denmark
christian-iv-of-denmark.summary: King of Denmark and Norway from 1588 to 1648, Scandinavia's longest-reigning monarch, remembered for ambitious reforms and for leading Denmark–Norway into the costly Thirty Years' War.

christian-ii-of-denmark.name: Christian II of Denmark
christian-ii-of-denmark.summary: King of Denmark and Norway from 1513 to 1523 and briefly King of Sweden in 1520–21, whose bloody purge of Swedish nobles led to his deposition and eventual lifelong imprisonment.

stockholm-bloodbath.name: Stockholm Bloodbath
stockholm-bloodbath.summary: A trial and series of executions in Stockholm on 7–9 November 1520, following King Christian II's coronation, in which nearly 100 people, many of them nobles, were killed despite promises of amnesty.

frederick-ii-of-denmark.name: Frederick II of Denmark
frederick-ii-of-denmark.summary: King of Denmark and Norway from 1559 to 1588, whose reign brought peace and prosperity after his father's civil war, with building projects at Kronborg and Frederiksborg; father of Christian IV.

erik-xiv.name: Erik XIV
erik-xiv.summary: King of Sweden from 1560, who expanded Swedish power in the Baltic and fought Denmark, but showed growing mental instability and was deposed and later likely murdered in 1577.

kalmar-union.name: Kalmar Union
kalmar-union.summary: A personal union joining Denmark, Sweden and Norway (with Norway's colonies) under one monarch from 1397 to 1523, agreed at Kalmar and designed by Queen Margaret of Denmark.

klas-horn.name: Klas Horn
klas-horn.summary: Finnish-born Swedish nobleman and naval admiral (1517–1566) who fought for Sweden in the Northern Seven Years' War of 1563–1570.

resund.name: Øresund
resund.summary: A strait separating Denmark from Sweden that links the Baltic Sea to the Atlantic Ocean, one of the world's busiest waterways.

swedish-war-of-liberation.name: Swedish War of Liberation
swedish-war-of-liberation.summary: A 1521–1523 rebellion led by Gustav Vasa against King Christian II that ended the Kalmar Union joining Sweden, Norway and Denmark.

frederick-i-of-denmark.name: Frederick I of Denmark
frederick-i-of-denmark.summary: King of Denmark and Norway from 1523/1524 until his death in 1533, and earlier co-duke of Schleswig and Holstein, who won the throne after a war against Christian II.

christian-iii-of-denmark.name: Christian III of Denmark
christian-iii-of-denmark.summary: King of Denmark from 1534 and Norway from 1537 until his death in 1559, who made Lutheranism the state religion and became the first king of Denmark–Norway.

bornholm.name: Bornholm
bornholm.summary: A Danish island in the Baltic Sea, strategically located and fought over for centuries, usually ruled by Denmark but also by Sweden and Lübeck.

varberg.name: Varberg
varberg.summary: A coastal town in Halland County, Sweden, known today for its sandy beaches, contested between Sweden and Denmark in 16th-century wars.

daniel-rantzau.name: Daniel Rantzau
daniel-rantzau.summary: Danish-German field marshal (1529–1569) known for leading forces in the Northern Seven Years' War and the 1559 conquest of Dithmarschen.

battle-of-axtorna.name: Battle of Axtorna
battle-of-axtorna.summary: A battle fought on 20 October 1565 at Axtorna in south-western Sweden between the Kingdom of Sweden and Denmark-Norway.

sound-dues.name: Øresund toll
sound-dues.summary: A toll on ships using the Øresund strait between Denmark and Sweden, introduced in 1429 and providing up to two-thirds of Denmark's state income in the 16th–17th centuries.

cardinal-richelieu.name: Cardinal Richelieu
cardinal-richelieu.summary: A French Catholic cardinal and statesman who served as Louis XIII's chief minister from 1624 to 1642, strengthening royal power and opposing Habsburg influence during the Thirty Years' War.

mecklenburg.name: Mecklenburg
mecklenburg.summary: A historical region in northern Germany, ancestral seat of the House of Mecklenburg, whose largest cities are Rostock, Schwerin and Wismar.

herluf-trolle.name: Herluf Trolle
herluf-trolle.summary: Danish naval officer and Admiral of the Fleet (1516–1565) who co-founded the Herlufsholm boarding school in Zealand, Denmark.

bohus-fortress.name: Bohus Fortress
bohus-fortress.summary: A fortress in Kungälv, Sweden, on a high cliff by the Göta river, formerly situated on the old Norwegian–Swedish border.

bohusl-n.name: Bohuslän
bohusl-n.summary: A Swedish coastal province bordering Norway, held as a Norwegian territory from the 870s until ceded to Sweden by the 1658 Treaty of Roskilde.

gothicism.name: Gothicism
gothicism.summary: A Swedish cultural movement begun by 16th-century writers claiming the Goths originated in Sweden; it held influence through the 17th century and revived with 19th-century Romantic nationalism.

christiern-pedersen.name: Christiern Pedersen
christiern-pedersen.summary: A Danish canon, humanist scholar, writer, printer and publisher (c. 1480–1554).

poul-helgesen.name: Poul Helgesen
poul-helgesen.summary: A Danish Carmelite monk, humanist and historian (c. 1485 – died after 1534) who first supported Christian II and Lutheran reform but later broke with both, warning against the king and Lutheran preachers.

georg-stiernhielm.name: Georg Stiernhielm
georg-stiernhielm.summary: Swedish civil servant, mathematician, linguist and poet (1598–1672), called 'the father of the Swedish skald art' and best known for his hexameter poem Hercules.

johannes-magnus.name: Johannes Magnus
johannes-magnus.summary: Last functioning Catholic Archbishop in Sweden (1488–1544), and also a theologian, genealogist and historian.

olaus-magnus.name: Olaus Magnus
olaus-magnus.summary: A Swedish writer, cartographer and Catholic clergyman, born Olof Månsson, who lived from 1490 to 1557.

jesper-swedberg.name: Jesper Svedberg
jesper-swedberg.summary: Jesper Swedberg: A bishop of Skara, Sweden (1653–1735) and one of its most notable churchmen, who published the first Swedish hymn book in 1694; father of scientist Emanuel Swedenborg.

haquin-spegel.name: Haquin Spegel
haquin-spegel.summary: A Swedish religious author and hymn writer (1645–1714) who held several bishop's seats.

olaus-verelius.name: Olaus Verelius
olaus-verelius.summary: A Swedish scholar of Northern antiquities, 1618 to 1682, who published the first edition of a saga and founded the Hyperborean School that led to Gothicism.

hervarar-saga-ok-hei-reks.name: Hervarar saga ok Heiðreks
hervarar-saga-ok-hei-reks.summary: A 13th-century legendary Norse saga combining older Germanic heroic tales of wars between Goths and Huns, including poetic sections on the sword Tyrfing and their great battle.

heimskringla.name: Heimskringla
heimskringla.summary: The best-known collection of Old Norwegian kings' sagas, written in Old Norse in Iceland and likely composed by Snorri Sturluson around 1230.

olaus-rudbeck.name: Olof Rudbeck
olaus-rudbeck.summary: Swedish scientist and writer (1630–1702), professor of medicine at Uppsala University, known for work in anatomy and linguistics and for founding Sweden's first botanical garden.

thomas-kingo.name: Thomas Kingo
thomas-kingo.summary: A Danish bishop and hymnwriter (1634–1703) whose poetry marked the peak of Danish baroque literature.

eric-julius-bi-rner.name: Eric Julius Björner
eric-julius-bi-rner.summary: Swedish state official and scholar of ancient history, born in 1696 and died in 1750.

v-lsunga-saga.name: Völsunga saga
v-lsunga-saga.summary: A late 13th-century Old Norse prose saga telling the legendary origin and decline of the Völsung clan, including the story of Sigurd and the dragon Fáfnir.

tale-of-ragnar-lodbrok.name: Ragnars saga loðbrókar
tale-of-ragnar-lodbrok.summary: A 13th-century Icelandic legendary saga about the Viking ruler Ragnar Lodbrok, covering his marriages, his sons' exploits, and his death.

johan-fredrik-peringski-ld.name: Johan Fredrik Peringskiöld
johan-fredrik-peringski-ld.summary: Swedish translator (1689–1720) who succeeded his father as translator at the archive of antiquities, and also interpreted Adam of Bremen's description of Sweden and Jordanes' Getica.

s-gubrot-af-nokkrum-fornkonungum.name: Sögubrot af nokkrum fornkonungum
s-gubrot-af-nokkrum-fornkonungum.summary: A fragmentary Old Icelandic text about legendary Swedish and Danish kings, believed to be part of a younger, more entertaining redaction of the lost Skjöldunga saga written around 1250.

smundar-saga-kappabana.name: Ásmundar saga kappabana
smundar-saga-kappabana.summary: A legendary Icelandic saga about Asmund the Champion-Killer, essentially an adaptation of the German Hildebrandslied with material from the Tyrfing Cycle.

tycho-brahe.name: Tycho Brahe
tycho-brahe.summary: Danish astronomer (1546–1601) whose unprecedentedly accurate observations helped turn astronomy into a modern science; he built the observatory Uraniborg on the island of Hven.

uraniborg.name: Uraniborg
uraniborg.summary: An astronomical observatory and alchemy laboratory built around 1576–1580 by Tycho Brahe on the island of Ven, the first custom-built observatory in modern Europe.

ven-sweden.name: Ven
ven-sweden.summary: A small Swedish island in the Öresund strait, known as the site of Tycho Brahe's Renaissance-era observatories Uraniborg and Stjärneborg.

anders-celsius.name: Anders Celsius
anders-celsius.summary: A Swedish astronomer, physicist and mathematician (1701–1744), professor at Uppsala University, who proposed the centigrade temperature scale in 1742, later renamed after him.

pierre-louis-maupertuis.name: Pierre Louis Maupertuis
pierre-louis-maupertuis.summary: French mathematician and philosopher (1698–1759) who led an expedition to Lapland to measure the Earth's shape and formulated the principle of least action.

isaac-newton.name: Isaac Newton
isaac-newton.summary: English mathematician and physicist (1642–1727) whose 1687 Principia established the laws of motion and universal gravitation, founding classical mechanics.

ole-r-mer.name: Ole Rømer
ole-r-mer.summary: Danish astronomer (1644–1710) who in 1676 first showed that light travels at a finite speed, and who also invented the modern two-point thermometer.

io-moon.name: Io
io-moon.summary: The innermost of Jupiter's four Galilean moons, slightly larger than Earth's Moon and the most volcanically active body in the Solar System.

carl-linnaeus.name: Carl Linnaeus
carl-linnaeus.summary: Swedish biologist and physician (1707–1778) who formalized binomial nomenclature, the modern system of naming organisms, and is known as the father of modern taxonomy.

systema-naturae.name: Systema Naturae
systema-naturae.summary: A major work by Swedish naturalist Carl Linnaeus, first published in 1735, that introduced the Linnaean system of naming and classifying living things.

binomial-nomenclature.name: Binomial nomenclature
binomial-nomenclature.summary: A formal two-part system for naming species, credited to Carl Linnaeus and effectively begun with his 1753 work Species Plantarum.

uppsala.name: Uppsala
uppsala.summary: Sweden's fourth-largest city, the ecclesiastical centre of the country since 1164, and seat of Scandinavia's oldest university, founded in 1477.

royal-society-of-sciences-in-uppsala.name: Royal Society of Sciences in Uppsala
royal-society-of-sciences-in-uppsala.summary: The oldest of Sweden's royal academies, founded in Uppsala in 1710; early members included Emanuel Swedenborg and Anders Celsius.
royal-society-of-sciences-in-uppsala.source_title: Royal Society of Sciences in Uppsala

nicolas-steno.name: Nicolas Steno
nicolas-steno.summary: Danish scientist (1638–1686), later a Catholic bishop, considered a founder of modern geology and stratigraphy for his work on fossils and rock formation.

stratigraphy.name: Stratigraphy
stratigraphy.summary: A branch of geology that studies layers of rock to interpret sedimentary and volcanic rock formations and their age.

ptolemy.name: Ptolemy
ptolemy.summary: A Greco-Roman scholar of the 2nd century AD who wrote influential works on astronomy, geography and astrology; his geocentric model of the universe, promoted by the Catholic Church, was studied for over a thousand years.

nicolaus-copernicus.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
nicolaus-copernicus.summary: Renaissance polymath (1473–1543) who proposed that the Sun, not Earth, is at the center of the universe, triggering the Copernican Revolution.

tychonic-system.name: Tychonic system
tychonic-system.summary: Model of the universe published by Tycho Brahe in 1588 with Earth at the center, the Sun and Moon orbiting it, and the other planets orbiting the Sun.

paul-wittich.name: Paul Wittich
paul-wittich.summary: German mathematician and astronomer (c.1546–1586) whose geoheliocentric model may have directly inspired Tycho Brahe's own model of planetary motion.

olof-hiorter.name: Olof Hiorter
olof-hiorter.summary: Swedish astronomer (1696–1750) who studied auroras alongside Anders Celsius and was the first to link them to disturbances in Earth's magnetic field.

emanuel-swedenborg.name: Emanuel Swedenborg
emanuel-swedenborg.summary: A Swedish scientist and inventor who, after a spiritual phase beginning in 1741 that culminated in a revelation, became a Christian theologian and mystic best known for his book on the afterlife, Heaven and Hell.

charles-xii-of-sweden.name: Charles XII of Sweden
charles-xii-of-sweden.summary: King of Sweden from 1697 to 1718 who led Swedish forces to repeated victories against a much larger coalition in the Great Northern War, including at Narva in 1700.

lund.name: Lund
lund.summary: A city in southern Sweden founded around 990, seat of a Catholic archbishopric from 1103 and home to Lund University, established in 1666.

christopher-polhem.name: Christopher Polhem
christopher-polhem.summary: Swedish scientist, inventor and industrialist (1661–1751), ennobled by King Charles XII for his contributions to Swedish technological development, especially mining.

swedish-board-of-mines.name: Swedish Board of Mines
swedish-board-of-mines.summary: A Swedish government agency active from 1637 to 1857 that oversaw mining and metal processing and issued charters for furnaces and forges.

gustav-vasa.name: Gustav I (Gustav Vasa)
gustav-vasa.summary: King of Sweden from 1523 to 1560, he led the Swedish War of Liberation against Denmark, ended the Kalmar Union, and began the Protestant Reformation in Sweden.

j-mtland.name: Jämtland
j-mtland.summary: Historical province in central Sweden, originally an independent republic with its own law and currency; conquered by Norway in 1178 and ceded to Sweden in 1645.

h-rjedalen.name: Härjedalen
h-rjedalen.summary: Historical province in central Sweden bordering Norway, originally Norwegian territory ceded to Sweden in the 1645 Treaty of Brömsebro.

gotland.name: Gotland
gotland.summary: Sweden's largest island and a province in the Baltic Sea, home to about 61,000 people, most in its main town, Visby.

saaremaa.name: Saaremaa
saaremaa.summary: The largest island in Estonia, in the Baltic Sea, known by the name Ösel in most of the world from the 13th century until the 20th century.

treaty-of-roskilde.name: Treaty of Roskilde
treaty-of-roskilde.summary: 1658 treaty forcing a defeated Denmark–Norway to cede a third of its territory to Sweden during the Second Northern War.

treaty-of-copenhagen-1660.name: Treaty of Copenhagen (1660)
treaty-of-copenhagen-1660.summary: A 1660 treaty ending the Second Northern War between Sweden and the allied Denmark–Norway and Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, following up on the Treaty of Roskilde.

scania.name: Scania
scania.summary: Southernmost historical province of Sweden, roughly matching modern Skåne County; part of Denmark until ceded to Sweden by the 1658 Treaty of Roskilde.

blekinge.name: Blekinge
blekinge.summary: One of Sweden's traditional provinces, on the southern Baltic coast, and the smallest Swedish province located on the mainland.

halland.name: Halland
halland.summary: A traditional province on the western coast of southern Sweden, bordering the Kattegat sea; part of the Kingdom of Denmark until 1645.

saint-thomas-u-s-virgin-islands.name: Saint Thomas
saint-thomas-u-s-virgin-islands.summary: The second-largest of the three main U.S. Virgin Islands, home to the territorial capital and port of Charlotte Amalie.

saint-john-u-s-virgin-islands.name: Saint John
saint-john-u-s-virgin-islands.summary: The smallest of the three main U.S. Virgin Islands, located near Saint Thomas, with about 60% of it protected as a national park since 1956.

saint-croix.name: Saint Croix
saint-croix.summary: Caribbean island and the largest of the U.S. Virgin Islands, known for its two towns, Frederiksted and Christiansted.

new-sweden.name: New Sweden
new-sweden.summary: A Swedish colony along the lower Delaware River from 1638 to 1655, part of Sweden's efforts to colonize the Americas during the Thirty Years' War, until the Dutch conquered it.

saint-barth-lemy.name: Saint Barthélemy
saint-barth-lemy.summary: A French Caribbean island near Saint Martin, briefly a Swedish colony for nearly a century before returning to French rule after an 1877 referendum; its capital is Gustavia.

norse-settlement-of-north-america.name: Norse settlements in Greenland
norse-settlement-of-north-america.summary: Norse colonies on Greenland's west coast that peaked at 2,000 to 3,000 people, sustained by farming and walrus-ivory exports, lasting from the late 10th century until they disappeared by the 15th century.

kattegat.name: Kattegat
kattegat.summary: A sea of about 24,000 km² between Denmark and Sweden, through which the Baltic Sea drains toward the Skagerrak.

royal-academy-of-turku.name: Royal Academy of Turku
royal-academy-of-turku.summary: Finland's first university, founded in 1640 while Finland was part of Sweden; it later relocated to Helsinki and eventually became the University of Helsinki in 1917.

finland-under-swedish-rule.name: Swedish Finland
finland-under-swedish-rule.summary: The period when Finland was part of Sweden, from the Middle Ages until 1809, when it was ceded to Russia after the Finnish War.

proto-indo-european-mythology.name: Proto-Indo-European mythology
proto-indo-european-mythology.summary: The reconstructed body of myths and gods of the Proto-Indo-Europeans, inferred from shared elements across Indo-European traditions, including a sky father and dawn goddess.

germanic-mythology.name: Germanic mythology
germanic-mythology.summary: The body of myths native to the Germanic peoples, including Norse, Anglo-Saxon and Continental Germanic traditions, forming a key part of Germanic paganism.

martin-luther-university-halle-wittenber.name: University of Wittenberg
martin-luther-university-halle-wittenber.summary: A university founded in 1502 where Martin Luther was a professor; it merged with the University of Halle in 1817 to form Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg.

tors-ker-witch-trials.name: Torsåker witch trials
tors-ker-witch-trials.summary: Largest witch trial in Swedish history, held in 1675 in Torsåker parish, where 71 people were beheaded and burned in a single day.

galdrab-k.name: Galdrabók
galdrab-k.summary: An Icelandic grimoire from around 1600 with 47 spells and sigils, compiled by four scribes and blending Latin, runic, and Icelandic magic with Christian and Norse invocations.

carl-michael-bellman.name: Carl Michael Bellman
carl-michael-bellman.summary: Swedish songwriter, composer and poet (1740–1795), a central figure in the Swedish song tradition best known for his collections Fredman's Epistles and Fredman's Songs.

louisa-ulrika-of-prussia.name: Louisa Ulrika
louisa-ulrika-of-prussia.summary: Queen of Sweden from 1751 to 1771, married to King Adolf Frederick, and later queen mother during the reign of her son Gustav III.

gustav-iii.name: Gustav III
gustav-iii.summary: King of Sweden from 1771 until his assassination in 1792, who seized royal power from the nobility in a 1772 coup and was a major patron of the arts.

swedish-academy.name: Swedish Academy
swedish-academy.summary: Founded in 1786 by King Gustav III, this Swedish institution of 18 lifelong members is best known for choosing the Nobel Prize in Literature laureates.

nationalmuseum.name: Nationalmuseum
nationalmuseum.summary: Sweden's national gallery of fine arts in Stockholm, founded in 1792 as the Royal Museum and renamed when its current building opened in 1866, with benefactors including King Gustav III.

swedish-national-heritage-board.name: Swedish National Heritage Board
swedish-national-heritage-board.summary: A Swedish government agency responsible for protecting World Heritage Sites and other national historic monuments and environments.

scandinavia_baltic-early_modern-art-003: Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts
scandinavia_baltic-early_modern-art-005: Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts
scandinavia_baltic-early_modern-art-006: Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts
scandinavia_baltic-early_modern-art-008: Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts
scandinavia_baltic-early_modern-science-: Royal Society of Sciences in Uppsala
